text:
maria: Quick sync — we need to pick a sequencing approach for packaging/reserved paths. Large fintech says they'll sign if we offer dedicated + 99.95 SLA, but ops costs look scary. Thoughts?

devon: Can we get an ask doc from the customer? exact throughput + p95 targets matter a lot.

anya: They gave an RPS range and monthly token estimate in the sales thread. Rough numbers: 50 rps peak, 40M tokens/mo.

lee: 99.95% with dedicated pools => nontrivial capacity reservation and overprovision. We'll need autoscaling + warm pools. Ops cost roughly +30-45% for that footprint.

maria: So tradeoff is near-term revenue vs long-term unit economics/complexity. Proposal: run lightweight RICE per path (reserved vs payg + burst) with standardized inputs. Use conservative confidence.

cory: Agree. Also factor in support burden and onboarding time (sales cycle). Those hit timelines more than pure infra cost.

devon: Quick RICE calc example for this customer path:
```
Reach = 1 (this renewal)
Impact = 4 (enterprise logo + ref)
Confidence = 0.6
Effort = 2 (months of eng + infra)
RICE = (1*4*0.6)/2 = 1.2
```
That looks low if we only count one customer; bundling many similar customers changes reach.

anya: We should normalize Reach to deal size buckets (SMB, mid, enterprise) instead of per-customer. Sales can provide how many in pipeline.

lee: Operationally, we can offer a middle ground: reserved baseline + burst credits. Baseline gives the SLA; burst covers unexpected spikes. That reduces constant overprovision.

maria: How do we model pricing? Options: premium flat add-on for SLA vs committed monthly tokens with discount + SLA. Which is cleaner?

cory: Flat add-on easier for billing and quicker to launch; committed tokens requires quota tooling + contract terms. Both need telemetry changes.

devon: From implementation POV: flat add-on = change in billing + admission control check for SLA flag. Committed tokens = quota enforcement + usage accounting + proration logic. Est effort multiply.

anya: Revenue impact: committed tokens gives better predictability and higher ARR if sales can move customers there. Flat add-on likely smaller ARR uplift but faster conversions.

maria: For prioritization, let's define a single RICE template with standard Reach buckets, Impact mapping (1..5), Confidence default 60% for new enterprise asks, and Effort in engineer-months + ops. We'll ask eng to give estimates.

lee: I'll estimate engineering effort for both variants by EOD tomorrow. Will include infra runbook changes and SLO measurement.

cory: Ops will model cost delta (expected incremental GPU hours and headroom) — need the customer's qps + session lengths.

maria: Action items:
- maria: collect sales pipeline + deal size mapping (by Tue)
- devon: draft RICE template and run one example for this fintech (Tue)
- lee: eng infra estimate (EOD tomorrow)
- cory: ops cost model (Thu)
- anya: pricing sketch (flat add-on vs committed) + commercial implications (Thu)

rollout-bot: New file uploaded: "customer-fintech-rps-estimates.csv" (link)

devon: One more debate: gating launch behind infra (full quota enforcement) vs soft-launch (manual review + pilot). Soft-launch reduces time-to-revenue but increases manual ops. Thoughts? :thinking:

lee: Pilot is safer. We can do a 10-customer pilot with manual monitoring, then automate quotas after 1-2 months. That reduces blast radius.

maria: Agreed. Add pilot acceptance criteria: 1) stable p95 under promised SLA for 2 weeks, 2) no >1 incident needing manual scaling, 3) billing flows validated.

anya: Also require a rollback plan (automatic fallback to payg) if SLA breaches. Sales must sign runbook acknowledging behaviors.

cory: I'll draft the pilot runbook and incident playbook.

maria: OK—decision for now: run RICE with canonical inputs, prioritize the flat add-on + pilot path as fastest to close the fintech while we iterate on committed tokens for Q2. If committed tokens show much higher RICE, we ramp. Meeting Thu 10am to finalize numbers. :thumbsup:

devon: sounds good.

lee: 👍

anya: 👍

cory: 👍

maria: Thanks everyone — will post the RICE template and pipeline numbers in this thread when ready.
